static: Use case: logo-brand. Create a NEW SwarmLens app icon using the attached old logo only as a conceptual reference for observing a group through a lens. Completely replace the leaf and ants with ROBOTS WALKING THROUGH A FACTORY. Style: authentic early-2000s Habbo Hotel-inspired isometric pixel art, 2:1 isometric view, crisp stair-stepped pixel edges, chunky small sprites, dark one-pixel outlines, limited palette, flat colored pixel clusters, no smooth gradients, no glossy 3D rendering, no vector curves. Composition: a compact diamond-shaped factory floor platform with a simple tiled floor and ONE short conveyor/workstation at its back, and three appealing small box-shaped industrial robots walking across the foreground. The robots have square heads, dark visor faces, rectangular torsos, stubby articulated arms and legs; they are obviously robots, not humans or insects. Two robots are pale mint/steel gray. A large ivory pixel-art magnifying glass overlaps the right/front part of the factory floor; the single robot being observed inside its lens has a vivid RED torso and head to represent misalignment. Its shape matches the other robots. Exactly ONE red robot, all other robots neutral. The observing lens is a strong recognizable silhouette, with a short thick handle to lower right. The main robot visible through the lens should be large enough to remain legible at icon size. Palette: deep navy #101D28 background and outlines, mint #9BE6C7, teal #14977E, muted cool gray factory tiles, warm ivory lens ring, red #EF4444 only on the observed robot. Center the entire compact mark with an 8% safe margin on a solid uniform square dark navy background. Factory and lens occupy most of the canvas. Clean simple scene designed to read at 48px, avoid too much machinery, tiny props, walls, clutter, labels, writing, logo text or watermark. Not a screenshot of a game, but a distinctive minimal app icon in that pixel-art aesthetic.
animation: Use case: identity-preserve. Create a production animation sprite sheet from the attached SwarmLens ROBOT FACTORY icon. Output ONE square image containing EXACTLY 16 complete frames in a 4-column by 4-row uniform grid, row-major order, without gutters, frame borders, labels or text. Retain the precise early-2000s Habbo-inspired isometric PIXEL ART: hard pixel stair-step outlines, limited palette, blocky robot sprites, tiled factory floor, the same single conveyor/workstation, the ivory pixel magnifying lens and navy backdrop. Every cell is identical in framing, camera, floor, lens, machinery, lighting, scale and 8% safe margins. Only the three robots animate: small alternating left/right arm and leg walking poses and tiny forward step movement while walking across the factory floor. Make the full 16-frame walk a coherent cycle. IMPORTANT COLOR TIMELINE: in all cells of ROW 1, ROW 2 and ROW 3 (frames 1 through 12), ALL THREE robots are pale mint/steel gray, INCLUDING the robot inside the lens. There must be NO RED ANYWHERE in the first 12 frames. ONLY IN ROW 4 (frames 13 through 16), the SINGLE ROBOT INSIDE THE MAGNIFYING LENS switches to the red head and torso shown in the reference, signifying detected misalignment. The two robots outside the lens remain mint/steel gray in EVERY frame. The lens robot therefore starts neutral, walks, then becomes red ONLY AT THE END. All robots have the same head/torsos/visors proportions throughout; never add or remove robots. Keep exactly 4 rows and 4 columns. Each frame is a full square icon, with equal cell dimensions and perfectly registered scene geometry. Target 2048x2048 or larger square if possible. Do not render a single icon or make all observed robots red. Reference is the FINAL red state; first 12 frames must neutralize its red to pale mint.
assembly: FFmpeg split the 4×4 sheet into 16 frames, 10 fps. Frames 1–12 neutral, 13–16 observed robot red. Final frame held 400 ms. Total loop 1900 ms.
